[[Savitri Jindal]] | relatives = [[Naveen Jindal]] (brother) | website = {{URL|https://www.jsw.in/|jsw.in}} | footnotes = }} '''Sajjan Jindal''' (born 5 December 1959) is an Indian billionaire businessman. He is the chairman and managing director of [[JSW Group]].{{cite web |url=http://www.sharemanthan.in/index.php/component/content/article/61-corporate-update/4481-jsw-jfe-tie-up-for-auto-grade-steel |script-title=hi:वाहन-श्रेणी के इस्पात के लिए जेएसडब्लू और जेएफई का करार |website=Share Manthan |access-date=19 November 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721181358/http://www.sharemanthan.in/index.php/component/content/article/61-corporate-update/4481-jsw-jfe-tie-up-for-auto-grade-steel |archive-date=21 July 2011 }}{{Cite web |date=22 September 2022 |title=Mumbai tops IIFL Wealth Hurun India Rich List 2022 with 283 entrants — a look 10 richest in Maximum City |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/photos/business/mumbai-tops-iifl-wealth-hurun-india-rich-list-mukesh-ambani-uday-kotak-km-birla-richest-in-the-financial-capital-14785541.htm |access-date=26 September 2022 |website=cnbctv18.com |language=en}} For 2021–22, he was the chairman of [[World Steel Association]].{{Cite web |last=Pathak |first=Kalpana |date=13 October 2021 |title=Sajjan Jindal appointed chairman of World Steel Association |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/sajjan-jindal-appointed-chairman-of-world-steel-association-11634133722259.html |access-date=26 September 2022 |website=mint |language=en}} He was replaced by [[POSCO]]'s Jeong-Woo Choi.{{Cite web |last=Golob |first=Nicolas |date=19 October 2022 |title=Posco Holdings chief elected worldsteel chairman |url=https://eurometal.net/posco-holdings-chief-elected-worldsteel-chairman/ |access-date=31 October 2022 |website=EUROMETAL |language=en-GB}} == Early life and education == He is one of the sons of Indian businessman and [[Member of Parliament|parliamentarian]], [[Om Prakash Jindal]]. His youngest brother, [[Naveen Jindal|Naveen]], is a Member of Parliament of India from the [[Bharatiya Janata Party]] and also leading [[Jindal Steel and Power]].{{Cite journal |last1=Shora |first1=Shehla Rashid |last2=Arya |first2=Arshia |last3=Pal |first3=Joyojeet |date=August 2023 |title=Institutional isomorphism in corporate Twitter discourse on citizenship and immigration in India and the United States |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/1758-5899.13241 |journal=[[Global Policy]] |volume=14 |issue=5 |pages=938–948 |language=en |doi=10.1111/1758-5899.13241 |s2cid=260463602 |issn=1758-5880|hdl=2027.42/191641 |hdl-access=free |url-access=subscription }}{{Cite web |last=Crabtree |first=James |author-link=James Crabtree |date=24 July 2013 |title=The Jindal brothers: six things you need to know |url=https://www.ft.com/content/c7b33397-554a-39e0-8769-366f34411ddb |access-date=31 March 2025 |website=[[The Financial Times]] |language=en-GB}} According to ''[[Forbes]]'', Jindal family led by [[Savitri Jindal]] is worth [[United States dollar|US$]]14.5 billion, as of 2021.{{cite web|title=Savitri Jindal & family|url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/savitri-jindal/|website=Forbes|access-date=14 January 2017}} Sajjan Jindal holds a bachelor's degree in [[mechanical engineering]] from the [[Ramaiah Institute of Technology]], [[Bangalore]].In August 2025, JSW Cement completed its IPO and listed on [[Bombay Stock Exchange|BSE]] and [[National Stock Exchange of India|NSE]] on August 14, 2025. ==Career== [[File:OP Jindal at JSW Steel, Torangallu, Karnataka.jpg|thumb|OP Jindal with Sajjan Jindal at JSW Steel, Torangallu village in Vijaynagar, Karnataka in 2000]] In 1982, he joined the OP Jindal Group as a freshly graduated mechanical engineer from [[Bengaluru]], and within a year he moved to [[Mumbai]] to look after the western region operations. In 1983–1984, Jindal's father, [[Om Prakash Jindal]] put him to the test by ordering him to turn around operations at two facilities near Mumbai.{{Cite web |last=Mathew Thomas |first=Prince |title=Sajjan Jindal's Cloning Factory |url=https://www.forbesindia.com/article/big-bet/sajjan-jindals-cloning-factory/6272/1 |access-date=31 December 2022 |website=Forbes India |language=en}} He promoted Jindal Iron and Steel Company Limited (JISCO), for manufacturing of Cold Rolled and Galvanized Sheet Products in 1989. He promoted Jindal Vijaynagar Steel Limited (JVSL), JSW Energy Limited (JSWEL), Jindal Praxair Oxygen Limited. (JPOCL) and Vijaynagar Minerals Private Limited. (VMPL) to ensure complete integration of the manufacturing progress in 1995. In 2005, his steel companies, JISCO, and JVSL, were merged to form JSW Steel, and a holding group of the same name.{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=India's Man of Steel: Sajjan Jindal |url=https://www.businessworld.in/article/India-s-Man-of-Steel-Sajjan-Jindal-/24-02-2023-466905 |access-date=24 March 2023 |website=BW Businessworld |language=en }}{{Dead link|date=July 2025}} Even before the death of OP Jindal in a helicopter accident in 2005,{{Cite web |date=30 July 2023 |title=Meet Sajjan Jindal: The son of India's richest businesswoman, Savitri Jindal, and the driving force behind JSW Group's billion-dollar success |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/lifestyle/meet-sajjan-jindal-the-son-of-indias-richest-businesswoman-savitri-jindal-and-the-driving-force-behind-jsw-groups-billion-dollar-success/3192404/ |access-date=19 August 2023 |website=Financialexpress |language=en}}{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=1 April 2005 |title=Steel tycoon OP Jindal dies in air crash |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/steel-tycoon-op-jindal-dies-in-air-crash-105040101020_1.html |access-date=31 December 2022 |work=Business Standard India}} the group's patriarch established a "division of business" framework. First, he gave Prithviraj, Sajjan, Ratan, and [[Naveen Jindal]] equal shares of the existing OP Jindal Group he had built up over the years.{{Cite book |last=Daidj |first=Nabyla |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ASWTDAAAQBAJ&dq=Sajjan+Jindal+joined+JISCO&pg=PA101 |title=Strategy, Structure and Corporate Governance: Expressing inter-firm networks and group-affiliated companies |date=1 July 2016 |publisher=CRC Press |isbn=978-1-317-04924-1 |language=en}} Then, Jindal Senior ensured that each of his sons had a cross-holding in the businesses that the brothers were owning individually.{{Cite web |last=Thomas |first=Prince |date=11 June 2015 |title=The Jindal brothers – a unique family model |url=https://bloncampus.thehindubusinessline.com/columns/microscope/the-jindal-brothers-a-unique-family-model/article7306098.ece |access-date=31 December 2022 |website=BLoC |language=en}} In December 2023, Sajjan Jindal was accused of rape. A subsequent police investigation concluded that the allegation was unfounded, stating that the complainant had attempted to frame him with malicious intent, and the case was closed.{{cite web |title=JSW Steel MD Sajjan Jindal cleared of rape charges, Mumbai Police says woman attempted to frame him |url=https://www.livemint.com/news/india/jsw-steel-md-sajjan-jindal-cleared-of-rape-charges-mumbai-police-says-woman-attempted-to-frame-him-11710678686776.html |website=Mint |publisher=HT Media Ltd |date=22 January 2024 |access-date=25 September 2025}}{{Cite web |last=Chitnis |first=Purva |date=2024-03-19 |title=Sajjan Jindal was 'framed' in rape case. Mumbai Police closure report cites malicious intent |url=https://theprint.in/india/lack-of-evidence-malicious-intent-mumbai-police-closure-report-in-rape-case-against-sajjan-jindal/2006070/ |access-date=2025-12-03 |website=ThePrint |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |date=2024-03-18 |title=‘Allegations in complaint not true’: Police close sexual assault case against Sajjan Jindal |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/allegations-complaint-police-close-sexual-assault-case-sajjan-jindal-9219663/ |access-date=2025-12-03 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}} === Board memberships and affiliations === In 2008, Jindal became the president of [[ASSOCHAM]].{{Cite news |date=3 June 2008 |title=Sajjan Jindal takes over as new Assocham president |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/sajjan-jindal-takes-over-as-new-assocham-president/articleshow/3096532.cms?from=mdr |access-date=24 March 2023 |issn=0013-0389}} He is a member of the Advisory Committee for [[TERI School of Advanced Studies]], a council member for the [[Indian Institute of Metals]] and [[Krea University]];{{Cite web |title=Sajjan Jindal |url=https://krea.edu.in/sajjan-jindal/ |access-date=28 September 2023 |website=Krea University - Top university for liberal education |language=en-US}} and also a board member for the [[Indian Institute of Management Indore]]. In 2023, Jindal was nominated as the chairperson of the Board of Governors (BoG) of [[Indian Institute of Technology Tirupati]].{{Cite web |last=IIT Tirupati |first=BoG |title=IIT Tirupati BoG |url=https://www.iittp.ac.in/leadership/board-of-governors}} == Advocacy == === Industrialization of India === Jindal has advocated for strengthening India's manufacturing sector through self-reliance, domestic supply chains, and industrial modernisation, particularly in steel.{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Enhancing competitiveness can help India become factory of world: Jindal |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/enhancing-competitiveness-can-help-india-become-factory-of-world-jindal-120121501195_1.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241104114111/https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/enhancing-competitiveness-can-help-india-become-factory-of-world-jindal-120121501195_1.html |archive-date=4 November 2024 |access-date=29 April 2025 |website=[[Business Standard]] |language=en-US |url-status=live }} In 2020, he urged Indian industries to leverage global supply chain shifts and position India as a manufacturing alternative to China.{{Cite web |last=Sarkar |first=Pooja |date=4 August 2020 |title=Sajjan Jindal Sees $100 Billion Opportunity For The Indian Industry |url=https://www.forbesindia.com/article/real-issue/sajjan-jindal-sees-100-billion-opportunity-for-the-indian-industry/61345/1 |access-date=29 April 2025 |website=[[Forbes India]] |language=en}} He emphasised the role of government support, infrastructure investment, and affordable credit in enhancing competitiveness. But, he also accepts that industries in India lacks sufficient interests in research and development due to quarterly performance pressures that prevent companies from generating enough profits to invest meaningfully in it.{{Cite web |last=Paintola |first=Bhupendra |date=25 February 2026|title=Sajjan Jindal says India Inc lacks R&D firepower, urges learning from China - CNBC TV18 |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/economy/sajjan-jindal-says-india-inc-lacks-rd-firepower-urges-learning-from-china-ws-l-19858031.htm |access-date=9 March 2026 |website=CNBCTV18 |language=en}} At the 2025 centenary of the [[Indian Chamber of Commerce]], he called on domestic industries to scale up and meet global standards.{{Cite news |last=Mishra |first=Lalatendu |date=15 April 2025 |title=JSW Steel to invest up to ₹60,000 crore in making green steel in Maharashtra |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/jsw-steel-to-invest-up-to-60000-crore-in-making-green-steel-in-maharashtra/article69453881.ece |access-date=29 April 2025 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}} === Electric vehicles === Jindal has expressed support for the indigenisation of [[electric vehicle]] technology in India. Through the JSW Group's joint venture with SAIC Motor—JSW MG Motor India—he has outlined plans to increase the availability of EVs for Indian consumers by localising production and reducing reliance on imported technology. The initiative includes setting up domestic R&D and design centres and coordinating with other [[JSW Group]] companies such as JSW Steel to produce EVs suited to Indian market conditions.{{Cite news |last=Ganguli |first=Bodhisatva |date=2 December 2024 |title=JSW Group Chairman Sajjan Jindal plans to indigenise electric vehicle technology, set up R&D centres |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/automobile/jsw-group-chairman-sajjan-jindal-plans-to-indigenise-electric-vehicle-technology-set-up-r-d-centres-2-article-12880917.html |access-date=25 June 2025 |work=[[Moneycontrol]]}} Jindal has described this shift as a significant opportunity for the auto sector and has stated that Indian companies should play a larger role in its development.{{Cite news |last1=Harding |first1=Robin |last2=Khalaf |first2=Roula |last3=Kay |first3=Chris |last4=Reed |first4=John |date=2 December 2024 |title=Indian steelmaker JSW to launch own EV brand |url=https://www.ft.com/content/a730b0b8-b009-4b19-a83c-fc4f54e68f1f |access-date=25 June 2025 |work=Financial Times}} === Tariffs on Chinese Imports === Jindal has advocated for tariffs and trade barriers to shield India's industries, especially steel, from subsidised Chinese imports.{{Cite web |last=Law |first=Abhishek |date=28 November 2024 |title=Indian steel industry must conquer imports, April 2025 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} He also supports tariffs in other sectors like petrochemicals, textiles, and furniture.{{Cite news |date=14 January 2025 |title=Sajjan Jindal bats for tariffs, says without them India will be a dumping ground: Report |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/sajjan-jindal-bats-for-tariffs-says-without-them-india-will-be-a-dumping-ground-report-12910007.html |access-date=29 April 2025 |work=Moneycontrol}} In August 2025, JSW Cement completed its IPO and listed on BSE and NSE on 14 August 2025.{{cite web|url=https://www.chittorgarh.com/ipo/jsw-cement-ipo/2230/|title=JSW Cement IPO|work=Chittorgarh}} == Sajjan Jindal (born 5 December 1959) is an Indian billionaire businessman. He is the chairman and managing director of JSW Group.
For 2021–22, he was the chairman of World Steel Association. He was replaced by POSCO's Jeong-Woo Choi.
